statement: For taxable years beginning in 2026, the AMT exemption amounts under § 55(d)(1) are $140,200 (joint returns/surviving spouses), $90,100 (unmarried individuals), $70,100 (married filing separately), and $31,400 (estates and trusts); under § 55(d)(2), as amended by P.L. 119-21 § 70107, the exemption phases out at 50 cents per dollar above threshold AMTI of $1,000,000 (joint; completely phased out at $1,280,400), $500,000 (unmarried; complete at $680,200), $500,000 (MFS; complete at $640,200), and $104,800 (estates/trusts; complete at $167,600); and the 28% rate applies to excess taxable income above $244,500 ($122,250 MFS), with 26% below (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 2.10, applying § 55(b)(1) and § 55(d)).
caveat: 2026 amounts only — these adjust annually and the later year's revenue procedure controls later years. P.L. 119-21 § 70107 reset the phaseout thresholds and doubled the phaseout rate to 50 cents per dollar for taxable years beginning after 2025; the complete-phaseout figures confirm that arithmetic (threshold + exemption/0.50). Any use of these figures is an illustration, never a filing computation.
